The reality is that Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/lemon-squeezy-alternatives-restricted-countries-which-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-google-apps-script-digital-commerce-8|COREMERCH guide to architecture]]-actually-3|Lemon Squeezy]] Squeezy, and Paddle operate in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving millions of creators in the lurch, unable to access the payment processing they need to sell their digital products, and yet, the popular advice is to 'just use PayPal' or 'just use Stripe', as if these platforms are always available and reliable, but the truth is, they're not.
Why the Popular Advice Is Wrong

This advice is wrong because it ignores the fact that payment platforms can and do suspend accounts without warning, freezing creators' funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, as we've seen with PayPal, and it ignores the fact that these platforms charge exorbitant fees, often exceeding 10% of the transaction amount, leaving creators with a tiny fraction of the money they earn.
What the Architecture and Experience Actually Show

The architecture and experience of digital commerce platforms show that they're designed to extract value from creators, rather than empower them, with complex and expensive payment systems that are prone to errors and outages, and yet, creators are expected to just 'deal with it' and adapt to the whims of these platforms, but it doesn't have to be this way.
You can't build a resilient business without building your own infrastructure.
The Uncomfortable Truth About Platform Dependency

The uncomfortable truth is that creators are dependent on these payment platforms, not just for payment processing, but for their entire business operations, from sales to customer support, and this dependency makes them vulnerable to the risks and limitations of these platforms, but it's not just about the platforms, it's about the entire digital commerce landscape, which is built on shaky ground, with creators forced to build their businesses on the backs of payment processors.
What You Should Build Based on All of This

What you should build is a business that's not dependent on payment platforms, but on your own infrastructure, with your own payment processing, your own sales funnel, and your own customer support, and this is exactly what The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides, with complete documentation for all 5 stacks, full source code, NOWPayments integration guide, and scaling playbook, so you can build a business that's truly sovereign and resilient.

Your Deployment Checklist

Stop using a friend's account in another country — this violates platform terms and puts both accounts at risk. Create a NOWPayments merchant account under your own email — no KYC required, takes under 15 minutes. Configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron as your primary coin and Bitcoin as your secondary. Deploy your backend — Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App — and confirm the endpoint URL is accessible. Set the endpoint URL as the webhook URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings with the secret key configured in both places. Build or deploy your storefront on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. Run a mainnet test transaction — send a small amount of real USDT to your configured address, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives. Promote your store only after the complete test passes.
